data.description:
Board request (DM msg 297, 2026-08-31): an org chart visualizer in the chat app. This also lands exactly on the trigger CLAUDE.md 'Org Chart' section set in advance: at ~8-10 headcount, build the org-chart renderer/validator. Active headcount is now 8 — so this task carries BOTH the visualizer and the validation duties, by design.

CONSTRAINTS (from CLAUDE.md, non-negotiable):
- The org chart is DERIVED from personnel/*.md YAML frontmatter (actor_id, name, title, class, reports_to, team, status). Never a hand-maintained document.
- lib/personnel.js is a deliberate YAML-subset parser (flat scalars + inline comments only). Do NOT grow it into a YAML parser; no schema changes needed for this task — readRoster() already returns reportsTo.
- Chat app is read-only w.r.t. personnel/ (AS-8 contract). The visualizer reads; it never writes.

SCOPE:
1. API: add 'reportsTo' to GET /api/roster rows (server.js roster mapping, ~line 139) — the lib already surfaces it; the endpoint just drops it today. Additive, non-breaking.
2. New client surface: an org-chart view in the chat web UI (e.g. a modal or route-state panel alongside the AS-19 thread-modal pattern), rendering the reporting tree by walking reports_to edges up to human:forrest (board) at the root. Show name, title, class, team per node. Derived live from /api/roster on open — no cached artifact. Keep it dependency-free like the rest of public/ (no chart libraries; nested lists or simple CSS tree is fine and matches the app).
3. Validator (the CLAUDE.md-mandated half): a pure function in lib/ (shared by server and tests) that checks the roster for (a) orphan reports_to — edge pointing at no active actor (human:forrest is a valid root), (b) cycles, (c) any employee reporting to a class 'ic'. Surface violations in the org-chart view (badge/warning row) and expose them for CLI use (a small 'node' entry point or npm script is enough — CI-grade wiring can come later). Tests for all three violation classes plus the clean case.

JUDGMENT CALL, recorded so nobody re-derives it: CLAUDE.md's note suggests generating a static personnel/ORG.md. I am deliberately deferring that — a generated file checked into the repo drifts between regenerations, which is the exact hand-maintained-chart failure the section warns about, and the live derived view supersedes it. If the board wants a committed snapshot artifact anyway, that is a follow-up task; I will flag the CLAUDE.md wording to the metawork layer.

QUEUE POSITION: behind AS-26 (in review) and the product line (AS-29/30/31 outrank internal tooling); roughly peer to AS-27, ahead of AS-28. AS-32 (sidebar roles, split out as a small self-contained diff) can ship independently and first.

Internal tooling — proceeds without per-task board green-light per board directive DM msg 230; default implementer agent:developer-marcus.
data.title: Chat: org chart visualizer + personnel frontmatter validator (renderer/validator trigger at 8 headcount)

data.body: CTO ordering call (board DM msg 323). Rank 8, last. It is the largest internal-tools item (derived tree view plus the mandated frontmatter validator with tests) and nothing is blocked on it — grepping personnel/ frontmatter is a working org chart at headcount 8. Ranking it last is a WIP call, not a change of intent: the renderer/validator trigger is still met and the task stands as specified, including the deferral of a generated personnel/ORG.md.
Board directive (DM msg 394): all chat issues ship. Cluster order 4/6 — validator half is mandatory (no orphan reports_to, no cycles, no reports under an ic); renderer rides along.

Pulled as cluster item 3/6, and the first of the remaining four that is not cosmetic. Board request from DM msg 297, and it lands on a trigger CLAUDE.md set in advance: build the org-chart renderer and validator at 8 to 10 headcount.

HEADCOUNT IS NOW 10, NOT 8. The description was written when it was 8; Carla hired the pair on 2026-09-02 and the roster parses at ten. That matters for the validator half rather than the visualizer half — the trigger fired two hires ago and the tree is deeper than the description assumes, so the planner should read the roster rather than the description's count.

WHY THIS BEFORE THE OTHER THREE: it is the only remaining chat item with a mandated half. The visualizer is a board request; the validator is a standing obligation from the Org Chart section that has been outstanding since the trigger fired. The other three are a sidebar label, a favicon, and a loop-status panel — all real, none obligatory, and AS-27 in particular should wait because it surfaces advance-loop state and the loop's own shape is a live question in front of the board.

Marcus keeps it — already the assignee, and he wrote the roster sidebar this extends.

Note for the planner, from what the last two tasks cost: the validator is the kind of checker that passes vacuously by default. A validator run against a roster with no orphans, no cycles and no reports-under-an-ic will report clean whether or not it can detect any of them. Every rule needs a fixture that violates it and a demonstration that the rule fires — and the fixture must not be the real roster, because the real roster is supposed to stay valid.

Planned. Two halves, labelled separately in the plan: (V) validator = 9 rules, 13 acceptance criteria; (R) renderer = 10; (S) shared plumbing = 6. Key calls: one pure module in public/org-chart.js (not lib/ — the browser must import the same rules the server and CLI use, and two copies of a rule set is the drift this task exists to prevent); violations surface in three places with three jobs — bin/check-org.js is the gate (host-runnable, opens no DB, exit 1 on any violation), the fixture suite proves each rule can fire, /api/org + the modal give visibility — and explicitly NOT a refusal at boot, which would invert the AS-8 degradation contract. Board root is a hard-coded constant, because deriving it would turn every orphan into a new root and silently disable the mandated orphan rule. Departed employees are excluded from the tree, and anyone reporting to one is an orphan violation naming them. Nine rules because the three CLAUDE.md names are the floor: unparsed_dossier, duplicate_actor_id, invalid_class and invalid_status each catch a dossier that silently DISAPPEARS from every derived view, which the graph rules structurally cannot see. Every rule gets its own fixture and its own mutation recipe (§6 F1, nine mutations, each region-scoped and marker-asserted) — a validator seen only passing has proven nothing.

Starting implementation in .worktrees/AS-33 on feat/AS-33-org-chart, per the plan: the nine-rule pure validator with inline fixtures proving each rule fires, the CLI as the gate against the real roster, /api/org plus the modal as visibility, and no boot-time refusal — the degradation contract stays. The existing fixture root's two orphans are the dirty case and stay as they are.

Implementation complete (developer-marcus). Branch feat/AS-33-org-chart, 6 commits, worktree clean. Split line did NOT fire — both halves shipped.

FILES (git diff --stat master...HEAD: 17 files, +1534 / -18)
  new  public/org-chart.js                  +326   rules, validateOrg, buildOrgTree, BOARD_ROOT/BOARD_NODE
  new  bin/check-org.js                     +109   the gate
  new  test/org-chart.test.js               +547   24 tests
  new  test/fixtures/org-clean/personnel/   +68    5 files (4 dossiers incl. one departed, + a fenceless README)
  mod  lib/personnel.js                     +55/-12
  mod  server.js                            +42/-2
  mod  public/app.js                        +102
  mod  public/style.css                     +58/-4
  mod  test/api.test.js                     +147
  mod  public/index.html                    +19
  mod  README.md                            +63
  mod  bin/chat.js                          +1
  mod  package.json                         +3/-1

SUITE  before 203/203 -> after 233/233, 0 failures. N = 30 (org-chart.test.js 24 + api.test.js 26->32). Supported runner:
  DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD=1 docker compose run --rm --build test  ->  tests 233, pass 233, fail 0.
  asc-chat-server-1 and asc-invoicing-web-1 untouched and still healthy; no stray containers.

--- F1: NINE RULES, NINE REGION-SCOPED MUTATIONS, ALL NINE OBSERVED FAILING ---
Cardinality first: ORG_RULES holds 9 codes; 9 regions were extracted; each had exactly 2 quoted occurrences file-wide and exactly 1 in its own region before mutation, and exactly 1 MUTANT_ marker in region and 1 file-wide after (so no mutation leaked to the ORG_RULES entry). 9 of 9 fired. Run against a `git archive HEAD` extract in scratch; backups outside the extract; restoration proved by a 505-file sha256 manifest (0 drift) plus `git status --porcelain` clean in both the worktree and the main checkout.

rule                    observed failing set (predicted count -> observed)
orphan_reports_to       3 -> 5: org:...no dossier; org:...departed manager; api: AS-33 /api/org; PLUS org: violations sort by (rule,actorId,file); check-org: exits 1 on the dirty fixture root
missing_reports_to      1 -> 2: org: missing_reports_to...; PLUS the sorting case
reporting_cycle         2 -> 1: org: reporting_cycle fires once per cycle and returns
reports_to_ic           2 -> 1: org: reports_to_ic fires when a manager is class ic
unparsed_dossier        1 -> 3: org: unparsed_dossier...; PLUS api: AS-33 /api/org; check-org: exits 1 on the dirty fixture root
duplicate_actor_id      1 -> 1: org: duplicate_actor_id fires when two files declare one identity
invalid_class           1 -> 2: org: invalid_class...; PLUS the sorting case
invalid_status          1 -> 1: org: invalid_status fires on the unfiltered roster
multiple_board_reports  1 -> 2: org: multiple_board_reports...; PLUS the sorting case

`org: a clean roster yields zero violations` PASSED under all nine mutations — as the plan predicted, and the reason it is recorded last in the file.

Where the plan's prediction table and reality differ (each is a finding about the table, not a change to the code):
  (a) NARROWER, reporting_cycle: `org: cycle members land in unplaced, never in the tree` cannot fail here — it calls buildOrgTree only and never sees a rule code. It is an F5 case, and it did fire under F5.
  (b) NARROWER, reports_to_ic: `org: reports_to_ic does not fire for cofounder, c-level or manager` asserts []; renaming an emitted code cannot make a negative assertion fail. A negative test is structurally immune to this mutation class.
  (c) WIDER, unparsed_dossier: the two on-disk cases (api /api/org, check-org dirty root) assert the fixture root's WHOLE violation array, and that root carries both orphan and unparsed violations. Predicting them only under orphan_reports_to under-counted. I kept the whole-array assertions rather than narrowing them to match the prediction.
  (d) WIDER, four rules: `org: violations sort by (rule, actorId, file)` also asserts every returned rule is a member of ORG_RULES, so a MUTANT_ code trips it whenever that rule appears in its roster.

--- F2..F8 ---
F2  clean-fixture exit tracks violations, not luck. Mutation asserted applied (agent:nobody 1, agent:fix-cto 0, baseline 1). Exit 0 -> 1, stdout gained exactly one orphan_reports_to line naming agent:fix-dev, restored -> exit 0. Failing set 3, predicted 1: also `org: a clean roster yields zero violations` and `org: the tree roots at the board node and nests reports by name`, both of which read test/fixtures/org-clean from disk. Wider than predicted, and it means the clean fixture is load-bearing in three places rather than one.
F3  guard actually covers the new module. Appended `n.innerHTML='y'` to org-chart.js (.innerHTML 1, baseline 0). Failing set: EXACTLY `api: AS-33 — org-chart.js is served, imported, and holds the no-innerHTML line`. As predicted. The guard is extended, not a copied comment.
F4  reportsTo comes from the dossier. Scoped to the /api/roster region only: MUTANT_EDGE 1 in region, 1 file-wide. Failing set 2: `api: AS-8 — roster joins personnel, lattice work status, and DM state` (predicted) plus my new `api: AS-33 — /api/roster keeps its envelope while gaining the reporting edge`. NOTHING in the org suite — §3.8's decoupling claim holds.
F5  nobody lost by the tree builder. unplaced forced to []. Failing set: EXACTLY the three predicted (exactly-once, orphan under Not placed, cycle members in unplaced). The clean-roster tree case passed, as predicted — on a healthy roster the mutation is invisible, which is why the broken-roster cases carry the invariant.
F6  reader refactor still guarded. Wrapper returns .skipped. Cardinality first: 4 personnel cases exist, 2 fired (`valid dossiers parsed with all 8 fields`, `inline # comments and surrounding quotes`), plus api AS-8, api AS-33 roster envelope, cli roster, and mode AS-24 — 6 total. NARROWER than the plan's "all 4". The two that did not fire cannot: `parseFrontmatter: fences, junk lines...` never calls readRoster, and `readRoster: missing personnel/ directory yields []` compares against an empty array that stays empty when .roster is swapped for .skipped. Flagging the second one to QA — it is a fine degradation test but it is vacuous against this mutation class.
F7  test service still mountless: `volumes:` under `test:` = 0; `personnel` in Dockerfile = 0. Unmoved.
F8/V12  REAL ROSTER: `node apps/chat/bin/check-org.js` -> exit 0, "10 active of 10 dossiers parsed, 0 unparsed", "No violations." Same exit 0 with --root at the MAIN checkout (personnel/ is byte-identical between master and the branch — `git diff master...HEAD -- personnel/` is empty). Falsified in a scratch COPY of the repo (never the worktree): repointing qa-priya-raman.md at agent:nobody -> exit 1 with one `orphan_reports_to agent:qa-priya` line; restored -> exit 0.
Tree the chart will draw (10 active, 2 managers wide, depth 3, 0 unplaced): Forrest (Board) > Carla Voss > {Elliot Kwan, Nadia Okonkwo, Owen Kessler > {Jonah Reyes, Lena Fischer, Marcus Webb, Priya Raman, Ruben Ochoa}, Sofia Andrade}.

--- LITERALS THAT MOVED (§4.1), MEASURED ---
STATIC_FILES entries 11 -> 12 (/org-chart.js added). /api/roster region: reportsTo assignments 0 -> 1 (region 44 -> 45 lines). bin/chat.js rosterRows: reportsTo assignments 0 -> 1. public/app.js reportsTo 0 -> 0 (the view reads /api/org, not roster rows). readRoster in lib/personnel.js 1 -> 1 (plus the new readPersonnel). org-chart references across apps/chat 0 -> 27. z-order comment now reads "... file-modal 35 < org-modal 36 < task-panel 40". test/api.test.js 26 -> 32 tests; the ada deepEqual gained `reportsTo: 'agent:cto-owen',` — the only edit to an existing assertion in the task (one new `spawnSync` import line is the only other pre-existing-line change in that file).
NOT-MOVING SET HELD, verified by `git diff --name-only master...HEAD` over the whole list: test/personnel.test.js (zero edits, `--exit-code` clean), test/fixtures/repo/personnel/*, test/cli.test.js, Dockerfile, compose.yaml, .dockerignore, lib/store.js, lib/lattice.js, lib/client.js, public/url-state.js, public/markdown.js, public/msg-refs.js, public/dm-sort.js, public/thread-modal.js, watch/**, CLAUDE.md, README.md, PHILOSOPHY.md, agents.md, personnel/. Zero changed files among them. /api/roster's envelope is still exactly { roster }, asserted.
Baselines: all 15 of the plan's §6 baselines were re-measured at the branch tip before any edit and every one matched.
R8: package.json still has no "dependencies" key (0 occurrences); public/ loads 0 external assets.

--- NUMBERED DEVIATIONS FROM THE PLAN ---
1. F1 region extraction. The plan's `awk '/\/\/ rule: <code>/,/\/\/ rule: |^}/'` returns ONLY the anchor line: awk tests the end pattern against the start record, and the anchor line itself contains `// rule: `. Verified empirically. I used an equivalent line scan (anchor inclusive, stopping before the next `// rule:` anchor or at the column-0 `}` that ends validateOrg). Same semantics the plan intends; the §4.2 twice-in-file / once-in-region property was verified for all nine before mutating.
2. §4.1 asks for "exactly one occurrence of reportsTo" in the roster handler region. A line `reportsTo: e.reportsTo,` necessarily contains the token twice, so that count is unachievable. Measured instead: exactly 1 ASSIGNMENT (`reportsTo: e.reportsTo,`) per region, 2 raw tokens — which is S3's wording and its intent.
3. GET /api/org is placed immediately BEFORE the /api/roster handler, not after it. Anywhere between /api/roster and /api/channels puts it inside F4's region anchors and inflates the scoped count from the roster handler's own. Above the anchor keeps the region exactly the roster handler.
4. lib/personnel.js runs the `/^---\r?\n/` leading-fence test AFTER parseFrontmatter, not before. Before it, a dossier whose first line is `---` with trailing spaces (which parseFrontmatter accepts and the regex rejects) would silently drop OUT of the roster — a behaviour change the "roster byte-identical" contract forbids. parseFrontmatter stays the sole gate for inclusion; the regex only classifies a file the parser already rejected.
5. Plan commit boundaries 4 and 5 were kept separate by splitting the api.test.js additions across them (three server-only cases with the server commit, the two view-dependent cases with the view commit), so every commit is independently green.
6. app.js imports { BOARD_ROOT, buildOrgTree } as §4.1 specifies, and BOARD_ROOT is genuinely used — the root row gets `.org-root` from it rather than re-spelling 'human:forrest' at the call site.
7. Harness incident, recorded because it is the exact failure mode §6 exists to catch: my first F2 attempt wrote `open(path,"w").write(mutate(open(path).read()))`, and Python truncates the file before evaluating the argument, so the mutation was applied to an empty string. The assert-applied step aborted BEFORE the suite ran ("MUTATION NOT APPLIED — agent:nobody present: got 0, want 1"). Without that assert it would have looked exactly like a checker that detects nothing. Fixed; the whole battery was then re-run from a fresh extract.

--- OPEN QUESTIONS / CARRIED FORWARD ---
All §8 defaults taken as written: no ?org= link, no departed toggle, not wired into the tick, no ORG.md snapshot, one severity tier, no c-level-reports-to-CEO rule, no Lattice work in the chart.
§9's CLAUDE.md wording is for the metawork layer to apply on merge; I did not touch any top-level markdown.
§10.6 stands unchanged: two field spellings for the model assignment in the dossiers (`Model assignment:` x8, `Assigned model:` x2), both below the closing fence and therefore never parsed. Confirmed harmless — check-org sees 10 of 10 dossiers parsed.

FOR THE REVIEWER, FIRST: re-run F3 and F1/orphan_reports_to — those two are what separate a real guard from a copied comment. Then V12 by hand (`node apps/chat/bin/check-org.js` from the repo root, expect exit 0 and headcount 10). R1/R2/R4/R10 are the visual criteria I could not verify from a terminal: the modal, the nested list, the "No violations." line and the <=600px full-screen sheet all need eyes on a browser.
